1. Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited (e.g. TJC, CHAP, etc.).

The Applicants AdviniaCare Scallop Shell, LLC (“New Operator”) and 55 Scallop Shell, LLC (“New
Real Estate Owner”) (collectively, the “Applicant”), seek Change in Effective Control (“CEC”)
approval for the acquisition of the operations and real estate, respectively, of Elderwood of Scallop
Shell at Wakefield (“Elderwood” or the “Facility”), an 80 bed skilled nursing facility located at 55
Scallop Shell Way in South Kingston, Rhode Island (the “Property”). 981 Kings Town Road
Operating Company LLC (“Current Operator”) currently operates the Facility. 981 Kings Town
Road, LLC (the “Current Property Owner”) is the current property owner.

The Transaction

The New Operator will acquire the operations of the Facility pursuant to a Purchase and Sale
Agreement by and among 981 Kings Town Road Operating Company, LLC, as Current Operator,
981 Kings Town Road, LLC, as seller, and AdviniaCare Scallop Shell, LLC, as New Operator, and
55 Scallop Shell, LLC, as Purchaser, Dated as of December 23, 2025 (“PSA”). See Tab 14. Pursuant
the PSA, the New Operator will acquire the operations of the Facility and the New Real Estate Owner
will acquire the Property. Pursuant to a lease agreement (Tab 24), the New Operator will lease the
Property from the New Real Estate Owner.

The total purchase price for the operations and Real Estate is $8,500,000. The Applicant will finance
the Proposed Transaction with a $6,800,000 conventional mortgage, $500,000 sellers’ note, and
$1,200,000 equity.

As set forth in the PSA (Tab 14), the sellers’ note requires that, at closing, the Applicant provide the
Current Operator and Current Property Owner (collectively, the “Sellers”) with an executed
promissory note, pursuant to which interest shall be paid monthly for a term of 36 months at a rate
of 6% per year with the final payment consisting of a balloon payment of all accrued and unpaid
interest and principal. The promissory note will be secured by an assignment of leases and rent and
jointly and severally guaranteed by Yosef Meystel, David Berkowitz, and Benjamin Berkowitz.

The Applicant

The New Operator’s corporate manager is AdviniaCare, LLC. The members of the New Operator
are: Yosef Meystel Delta Trust (30.75%), David A. Berkowitz Delta Trust (30.75%), Benjamin
Berkowitz Revocable Trust (18.50%), Shraga Braun (10%), Leah Braun Trust (5%), Brian Goldfarb
(2%), Moriel Hamui (1%), Frederick S. Frankel Trust (1%), and Hadassa Spector (1%).

The New Real Estate Owner’s corporate manager is Advinia Properties, LLC. The New Real Estate
Owner’s members are: Yosef Meystel Delta Trust (30.75%), David A. Berkowitz Delta Trust
(30.75%), Benjamin Berkowitz Revocable Trust (18.50%), Shraga Braun (10%), Leah Braun Trust

(5%), Brian Goldfarb (2%), Moriel Hamui (1%), Frederick S. Frankel Trust (1%), and Hadassa
Spector (1%).

Yosef Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz – the principals of the Applicant – through an
affiliated entity, own and operate AdviniaCare Pawtucket and AdviniaCare Providence. The Rhode
Island Department of Health (“RIDOH”) approved the CEC applications for the operations of those
facilities on January 31, 2025. In fact, an affiliated entity began providing management services at
those facilities pursuant to a RIDOH-approved management agreement since February of 2023. Since
their management of those facilities, the annual survey outcomes for the facilities significantly
improved, the operators prioritized decreasing turnover in key positions, the operators were able to
eliminate all agency staff and worked collaboratively with the unions in those facilities and have
infused capital into the facilities. The Applicant will provide the same dedication to this Facility upon
approval of the CEC Application.

On December 3, 2025, Rhode Island Department of Health also approved the CEC Applications of
the Applicant’s affiliated entities to acquire five skilled nursing facilities owned by Athena Health
Care Systems – Heatherwood Rehabilitation & Health Care Center, Oakland Grove Health Care
Center, Orchard View Manor Rehabilitation & Nursing Center, Summit Commons Rehabilitation
& Health Care Center, and Waterview Villa Rehabilitation. That closing is currently scheduled to be
effective February 1, 2026.

Moreover, Mr. Meystel, Ben Berkowitz, and David Berkowitz own and/or operate a total of 113
licensed facilities in 7 states.

Ben Berkowitz is an owner operator of 15 nursing facilities and senior housing facilities in Florida
and Massachusetts, as well as an investor in facilities in other states. Specifically, he is the Chief
Executive Officer of Pointe Group Care, LLC (“PGC”), which is headquartered in Massachusetts.
PGC employs staff focusing on operations, accounting, clinical, business development, technology
and accounts receivable and payable. PCG takes pride in providing high quality short-term
rehabilitation, nursing, and long-term care.

David Berkowitz and Yosef Meystel are the founders of Aperion Care, Inc. (“Aperion Care”).
Aperion Care is an administrative and management company firm that partners with geriatric
healthcare facilities. It specifically provides management services to skilled nursing facilities and
assisted living communities throughout Illinois and Indiana. Mr. Meystel began his career in
healthcare as an Assistant Administrator at Brightview Care Center in Chicago, Illinois. Following
Brightview, Mr. Meystel was the Administrator for EMI/EKS Management, where he became the
Administrator for Emerald Park Health Care Center. In 2006, Mr. Meystel founded YAM
Management, LLC and in 2014 formed Aperion Care, Inc., for which he serves as a board member
and shareholder. Aperion Care and PCG are now subsidiaries of the Kesser Group.

David Berkowitz serves as the President of Aperion Care, Inc., as well as a director and a shareholder.
He began his career in healthcare in 2002 as an administrator in training at Sebos Nursing & Rehab.
David Berkowitz then served as an administrator at a number of other skilled nursing facilities. He
has ownership interest in the real estate and/or operating entities of many skilled nursing facilities
located throughout Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Massachusetts, Florida and Kansas.

Massachusetts and Rhode Island – overseeing the 13 AdviniaCare affiliated facilities in the area.

1. Please indicate the financing mix for the capital cost of this proposal. NOTE: the Health Services Council’s policy requires a
minimum 20 percent equity investment in CEC projects.


    Source             Amount              Percent    Interest Rate           Terms (Yrs.)
Equity*         $1,200,000                     14.12%
Debt**          $7,300,000                     85.88%
Lease
TOTAL           $8,500,000
* Equity means non-debt funds contributed towards the capital cost related to a change in owner or change in operator of a healthcare
facility which funds are free and clear of any repayment or liens against the assets of the proposed owner and/or licensee and that result
in a like reduction in the portion of the capital cost that is required to be financed or mortgaged.

** If debt financing is indicated, please complete Appendix E.

The Applicant acknowledges the Health Services Council’s (“HSC”) policy for a 20 percent equity investment in CEC projects.
However, the HSC should find the proposed debt/equity percentage acceptable here as the Applicant and the principals have
the requisite financial commitment to this facility, in addition to their other facilities in the State. In particular, without the
sellers’ note, the Applicant will finance the transaction with 20% equity and 80% debt. The sellers’ note is a short-term note
that requires the Applicant’s principals to personally guarantee the payments. Moreover, the Applicant’s affiliates own and
operate two other facilities in the state and are shortly closing a transaction to own and operate an additional five facilities in
Rhode Island. As a result, the Applicant will own seven facilities in Rhode Island and are financially committed to this facility
and successfully owning and operating this additional Facility in the state.

                                    Appendix C (CONT.)

5.     Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative
and operational policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care,
services, and accommodations, and a sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify
how the proposal would advance these areas:

a.     Resident’s physical environment:

      i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

       The Facility offers both shared and private accommodations for residents. Common
       areas are available for interaction with other residents when preferred.

     ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

       The Facility offers rooms with modern décor. The residential rooms can be
       decorated with the residents’ personal belongings to promote a more familiar and
       comfortable environment.

     iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s),
         laundry, activities;

       Laundry service is provided. While group activities are available daily, residents
       may also participate in their own self-directed activities and always have access to
       television, books, movies, card games, beauty/barber salon and religious services for
       many denominations.

     iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and
        gardening);

       The Facility offers many outdoor spaces, including, for example, a patio area.

b.     Resident-centered systems of care:

      i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and negotiated
        risk;

       The Facility offers a home-like and autonomous environment, while still
       maintaining appropriate physical security systems. The Applicant will ensure that
       the physical security system, including wander management systems on main exits
       and alarms on egress doors are current and operational.

     ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);




                                                24

===== PAGE 27 =====
       The Applicant works with residents to schedule their preferred times for waking,
       bathing, and going to bed. The residents are also able to schedule their daily
       activities throughout the day.

     iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);

       The Applicant encourages the residents to provide their preferred dining time and
       location, as well as their meal preferences. Applicant will provide an alternate meal choice
       and make snacks available throughout the day. The Applicant will offer a diverse
       nutritious menu that caters to personal preference, allergy needs, religious beliefs, and
       physical comfort. The dietary staff ensures that residents with restrictive diets are able to
       enjoy an assortment of different meals.

     iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

       The structured recreational program includes a wide variety of activities for residents. The
       Applicant encourages resident feedback on those activities so that they can consistently
       improve and update the offerings. As set forth above, in addition to group activities,
       residents also may participate in their own self-directed activities.

c.     Workforce administration:

      i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident services and
        foster relationship building?

       The Applicant will ensure that the Facility maintains appropriate staffing ratios on all
       shifts and in all units. Staffing assignments take into account staff capabilities and specific
       needs of residents. In order to ensure the appropriate coverage, the Applicant continuously
       monitors the census and the residents’ conditions.

     ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g. Registered nurses,
        Licensed Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

       The Applicant will minimize staff turnover through job satisfaction and financial
       incentives. Staff is encouraged to recognize the significant role that they play in each
       residents’ life. Any changes in staffing are discussed with the residents before
       implementation.

        3.5     Title Defects. Within ten (10) Business Days following Purchaser’s receipt of the
Title Commitment and the Survey (the “Title Objection Deadline”), Purchaser shall notify Seller
of any matters shown on the Title Commitment other than Permitted Exceptions and Removable
Exceptions (“Unpermitted Exceptions”) or shown on the Survey that, in Purchaser’s sole
discretion, determines renders the title of the Property uninsurable or unmarketable (such matters
referred to herein as the “Title Defects”). Purchaser shall be deemed to have accepted the condition
of the Title Commitment and Survey unless it has given Seller timely written notice as herein
provided, after which time any such Unpermitted Exceptions and Survey Defects shall be
Permitted Exceptions. After receipt of notice from Purchaser, Seller, in Seller’s sole discretion,
shall then have ten (10) Business Days to provide written notice to Purchaser as to whether Seller
elect to: (a) have such Unpermitted Exceptions removed from the Title Commitment, (b) correct
such Survey Defects, (c) with Purchasers’ prior written approval at Closing, have the Title
Company commit to insure over any Unpermitted Exception or Survey Defect, or (d) not remove
or correct any such Unpermitted Exceptions or Survey Defects. Seller shall be deemed to have
elected to have such Unpermitted Exceptions removed from the Title Commitment unless it has
given timely notice to Purchasers as herein provided. If Seller elects not to remove or correct any
such Unpermitted Exceptions or Survey Defects, then Purchaser may elect upon written notice to
Seller made within ten (10) Business Days after the later of the expiration of the permitted time or
the receipt of Seller’s notice that Seller has elected not to remove or correct the Unpermitted
Exceptions or Survey Defects to (i) terminate this Agreement by written notice to Seller (which
shall be deemed a termination pursuant to Section 17 of this Agreement) in which event the Earnest
Money Deposit shall be returned to Purchaser; or (ii) take the Real Property as it then is. Purchaser
may obtain an updated Title Commitment and Survey prior to the Closing and with respect to any


                                                  11

new matters appearing on such updated Title Commitment and Survey, Purchaser shall notify
Seller in writing of all Unpermitted Exceptions and Survey Defects within five (5) Business Days

Survey, and Seller and Purchaser shall follow the same procedure to correct said title and survey
defects and have the same remedies as described above in this Section 3.5.

                                          ARTICLE VI
                                        DUE DILIGENCE

        6.1      Due Diligence Materials. Within ten (10) Business Days of the Signing Date
(“Due Diligence Delivery Date”), the Selling Parties shall, if not already made available to
Purchaser Parties, deliver, cause to be delivered, or make available copies of the following
documents and materials pertaining to the Property and the Facility to the extent within Seller's
possession or control: title commitment/policy, instrument survey, site plans and specifications,
architectural plans, inspections, environmental/hazardous material reports, soils reports,
governmental permits/approvals, zoning information, Tax information and utility letters, Resident
roll, copies of service contracts, certificates of occupancy, corporate documents, financial records,
employment policies and materials, and such other similar materials relating to the Property's
physical and environmental condition, the Facility and the Business that Purchaser Parties may
reasonably request (collectively, the “Due Diligence Materials”). Within thirty (30) days of the
Signing Date, the Selling Parties shall deliver to Purchaser Parties a copy of all Disclosure
Schedules to this Agreement.

        6.2      Due Diligence Period. Purchaser Parties shall have a period of forty-five (45)
days, commencing on the Signing Date (“Due Diligence Period”) to review the Due Diligence
Materials, Disclosure Schedules provided by Seller Parties and conduct or cause to be conducted
any and all tests, studies, surveys, inspections, reviews, assessments, or evaluations of the
Property, including, without limitation, engineering, zoning, and environmental inspections and
review of all Due Diligence Materials (the "Inspections"), as Purchaser Parties deem reasonably
necessary, desirable, or appropriate. Purchaser Parties shall have the right to terminate
this Agreement upon written notice to Seller delivered at any time prior to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time
on the last day of the Due Diligence Period. If Purchaser Parties do not timely notify Seller of its
election to terminate this Agreement prior to 5:00 p.m. on the last day of the Due Diligence Period,
Purchaser Parties shall be deemed to have elected to proceed to Closing, subject to the terms and
conditions of this Agreement and the Earnest Money Deposit plus interest accrued thereon shall
become non-refundable. If Purchaser Parties elect to terminate this Agreement as provided in this
Section, Deposit Escrow Agent shall return the Earnest Money Deposit plus interest accrued
thereon to Purchaser Parties, and this Agreement shall terminate, and the parties shall have no
further liability hereunder (except with respect to those obligations hereunder which expressly
survive the termination of this Agreement).

        6.3    Purchaser Parties’ Access. At any time prior to Closing (including during the
Due Diligence Period), and at all times subject to Section 6.4 below, Purchaser and New Operator
shall have the right to enter upon and pass through the Property during normal business hours to
examine and inspect the same, as well as conduct reasonable tests, studies, investigations, and


                                                 16

===== PAGE 59 =====
surveys to assess utility availability, soil conditions, environmental conditions, physical condition,
and the like of the Property.

       6.4     Purchaser Parties’ Right to Inspect.

                (a)    In conducting the Inspections or otherwise accessing the Property,
Purchaser Parties shall at all times comply with all Laws of all applicable Governmental
Authorities and maintain insurance in the amounts and types as determined by the Selling Parties,
as applicable, and provide evidence of the same to Selling Parties prior to Purchaser Parties’ first
entry onto the Property to conduct any Inspection. In connection with such Inspections,
Purchaser Parties shall not: (i) unreasonably interfere with or permit unreasonable interference
with any Person occupying or providing service at the Property; or (ii) unreasonably interfere with
the Business of either of the Selling Parties (or any of the Residents) conducted at the Property or
unreasonably disturb the use or occupancy of any occupant of the Property.

                 (b)    Purchaser Parties, as applicable, shall schedule and coordinate all
Inspections or other access thereto with Selling Parties and shall give Selling Parties at least two
(2) Business Days prior notice thereof. Selling Parties shall be entitled to have a representative
present at all times during each such inspection or other access.

        6.5     Selling Parties’ Indemnification.           Notwithstanding the indemnification
provisions in Article XIX below, Purchaser agrees to indemnify and hold Seller and Current
Operator harmless from and against any and all Damages (as hereinafter defined) (including, but
not limited to, Seller and Current Operator’s attorneys' fees, costs and disbursements) incurred by
Seller or Current Operator arising from or by reason of Purchaser's access to, or Inspections of, the
Property, except to the extent such Damages are caused by or resulting from: (a) any acts or
omissions of Seller or Current Operator; (b) Seller or Current Operator's gross negligence; and/or
(c) any pre-existing, dangerous, illegal, or defective condition at the Property. The provisions of
this Section shall survive the Closing or earlier termination of this Agreement.

                                      ARTICLE XI
                                  ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE

        11.1 Accounts Receivable. Current Operator shall retain whatever right, title and
interest it may have in and to all outstanding accounts receivable with respect to the Facility which
relate to periods ending on or before the Closing Date, including, but not limited to, any accounts
receivable arising from rate adjustments which relate to a period ending on or before the Closing
Date even if such adjustments occur after the Closing Date (“Current Operator’s A/Rs”). Current
Operator acknowledges that New Operator owns all accounts receivable arising from services
provided by or at the Facility after the Closing Date (“New Operator’s A/Rs”).

        11.2 Receipts by Purchaser. In furtherance and not in limitation of the requirements
set forth in Section 11.1, payments received by New Operator on or after the Closing Date from
third-party payors, including, but not limited to, Medicare, Medicaid, VA, managed care and health
insurance, shall be handled as follows:

              (a)      If such payments either specifically indicate on the accompanying
remittance advice, or if Current Operator and New Operator agree that such payments relate to the
period ending on or before the Closing Date, they shall be forwarded by New Operator to Current
Operator, along with the applicable remittance advice, within five (5) Business Days after receipt
thereof; and

               (b)      If such payments indicate on the accompanying remittance advice, or if
Current Operator and New Operator agree that such payments relate to the period after the Closing
Date, they shall be retained by New Operator.

       11.3 Receipts by Current Operator. Payments received by Current Operator after the
Closing Date from third-party payors, including, but not limited to, Medicare, Medicaid, VA,
managed care and health insurance, shall be handled as follows:

                (a)    If such payments either specifically indicate on the accompanying
remittance advice, or if Current Operator and New Operator agree that such payments relate to the
period after the Closing Date, they shall be forwarded by Current Operator to New Operator, along
with the applicable remittance advice, within five (5) Business Days after receipt thereof; and

               (b)    If such payments indicate on the accompanying remittance advice, or if
Current Operator and New Operator agree that they relate to the period ending on or before the
Closing Date, they shall be retained by Current Operator.


                                                 20

===== PAGE 63 =====
        11.4 Other Receipts. If the remittance advice indicates or the parties agree that any
payment relates to periods both on or prior to and after the Closing Date, the party receiving the
payment shall forward the amount relating to the other party’s operation of the Business, along
with the applicable remittance advice, within ten (10) Business days after receipt thereof. If the
remittance advice does not indicate the period to which a payment relates or whether it is for
Current Operator or New Operator, or if there is no accompanying remittance advice, or the
payment is not otherwise identifiable using commercially reasonable efforts, and if the parties do
not otherwise agree as to how to apply such payment, then 100% of such payments received within
the first forty-five (45) days after the Closing Date shall be deemed to have been collected in
respect of Current Operator’s A/R due from the payee in respect of services provided on or prior
to the Closing Date. All such payments received in excess of the amount of Current Operator’s
A/R due from said payee and all such payments received after the forty-fifth (45th) day after the
Closing Date shall be deemed to have been collected in respect of New Operator’s A/R from said
payee. All such payments received by New Operator but which are deemed to be due Current
Operator under this Section 11.4 shall be forwarded by New Operator to Current Operator within
ten (10) Business days after receipt thereof, and all such payments received by Current Operator
but which are deemed to be due New Operator under this Section 11.4 shall be forwarded by
Current Operator to New Operator within ten (10) Business days after receipt thereof. All such
payments received by Current Operator which are deemed to have been collected in respect to
Current Operator’s A/R shall be retained by Current Operator and all such payments received by
New Operator which are deemed to have been collected in respect to New Operator’s A/R shall
be retained by Operator. New Operator shall pay to Current Operator any and all reimbursements
including retroactive rate adjustments, appeal settlements, and/or Cost Report settlements for all
cost report periods with fiscal years ended prior to the Closing Date that it receives after the
Closing Date.

       11.5    Accounting for Accounts Receivable.

               (a)     Attached hereto as Schedule 11.5(a) is a schedule of Current Operator’s
A/Rs listing by Resident the amount due on the date that is within sixty (60) days after the Signing
Date. As soon as reasonably possible but not later than fifteen (15) Business Days after the Closing
Date, Current Operator shall provide New Operator with a schedule of Current Operator’s A/Rs
listing by Resident the amounts due as of the Closing Date.

A/Rs using the same format of schedule as that provided by Current Operator pursuant to Section
11.5(a), and (ii) upon request, copies of all remittance advices relating to such amounts received
and other reasonable supporting documentation as may be required for Current Operator to
determine the New Operator’s A/Rs and the Current Operator’s A/Rs that have been paid. New
Operator shall deliver such accounting to Current Operator at the following email address:
KKenworthy@elderwood.com.

                (c)    For a period of six (6) months following the Closing Date or until Current

         18.4 Risk of Casualty Pending the Closing. If, between the Signing Date and the

(except for the amount of any deductible under any insurance policy held by Seller insuring the

insurance claims and proceeds with respect thereto (less sums theretofore expended in connection
with such fire or casualty, if any, by Selling Parties, including for temporary repairs or barricades)
(in which event Purchaser shall have the right to participate in the adjustment and settlement of
any insurance claim relating to said damage), and (2) credit Purchaser at Closing with an amount
equal to Sellers’ insurance deductible. If, at the time of Closing, the estimated cost of repairing
such damage is more than Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($200,000.00) as determined by an
independent adjuster, Purchaser Parties may, in its sole discretion: (i) terminate this Agreement by
notice to Selling Parties within ten (10) days after receipt of notice of such casualty (which shall
be deemed a termination pursuant to Section 17.1(a)(ii) of this Agreement); or (ii) proceed to
Closing by electing to assume the insurance claims and proceeds in accordance with this Section.
Seller shall not compromise, settle or adjust any claims to such proceeds without Purchaser’s prior
written consent, which consent will not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Seller agrees to give
Purchaser prompt notice of any damage or destruction of the Real Property in excess of $25,000
that Selling Parties receive prior to the Closing.

public authority, or any agency thereof, against the Real Property, or any part thereof, Seller shall
promptly give Purchaser notice of such proceeding. In the event a “material” portion of the Real
Property is taken by eminent domain, then Purchaser Parties shall have the right, within fifteen
(15) days after receipt of notice of such material taking, to terminate this Agreement (which shall
be deemed a termination pursuant to Section 17.1(a)(ii) of this Agreement). If Purchaser elects to
proceed to Closing despite said material taking (such election being deemed to have been made
unless Purchaser notifies Seller in writing to the contrary within fifteen (15) days after notice from
Seller to Purchaser of any taking), or if there is less than a material taking prior to Closing, there
shall be no reduction in or abatement of the Purchase Price, Purchaser shall be required to purchase
the Real Property in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and Seller shall assign to
Purchaser, without recourse, all of Sellers’ right, title and interest in and to any award made or to
be made in the eminent domain proceeding (in which event Purchaser shall have the right to
participate in the adjustment and settlement of such eminent domain proceeding). For the purpose
of this Section, the term “material” shall mean any taking of in excess of eight percent (8%) of the
square footage of the Facility or fifteen percent (15%) of the Real Property associated with the
Facility or which would: (i) adversely affect the Purchaser Parties ability after said taking to
operate the Facility in compliance with the licensed beds; or (ii) eliminate after said taking a means
of egress and ingress to and from the Facility to a public right of way; or (iii) cause the use of the
Facility after said taking to no longer be in compliance with all applicable zoning and building
rules, regulations and ordinances. Seller shall not compromise or settle any claims to such awards
without Purchaser’s prior written consent, which consent will not be unreasonably withheld or
delayed.

malpractice claims arising from conduct prior to the Effective Time, (ii) any Tax Obligation of the

limitations; and further provided, however, if at the expiration of the applicable period any claim
or assessment for indemnification has been asserted but not fully determined, or any audit or other
proceeding with respect to any Tax matter has been initiated, such period will be extended as to
such claim, assessment, audit or other proceeding until it is finally determined or concluded; and
(iii) any civil monetary penalties that arise from a survey by CMS which arise prior to the Effective
Date shall be subject the aforesaid indemnities for a period of thirty-six (36) months after the
Closing Date.

        19.4 Notice to the Indemnifying Party. Within fifteen (15) days after the (i) assertion
of any claim by a third-party (a “Third Party Claim”), or (ii) occurrence of any event not involving
a Third Party Claim (a “Non-Third Party Claim” and, together with a Third Party Claim, each a
“Claim”), giving rise to a claim for indemnification from a party (the “Indemnifying Party”) under
this Article, the other party (the “Indemnified Party”) shall notify the Indemnifying Party in
writing of such Claim setting forth the nature of the Claim and specifying in reasonable detail (to
the extent the same can be reasonably estimated or ascertained) the individual items and amount
of Damages, the date each such item was paid, suffered or arose, or if such Damages have not yet


                                                 39

===== PAGE 82 =====
been paid, suffered or incurred (such notice is hereinafter referred to as an “Indemnity Claim
Notice”); provided, however, failure to provide such notice shall not in any way serve to waive or
diminish the indemnification rights of the Indemnified Party, except to the extent the Indemnifying
Party shall actually be prejudiced by such failure.

        19.5 Non-Third Party Claims. Within thirty (30) days after receipt of an Indemnity
Claim Notice, the Indemnifying Party shall furnish to the Indemnified Party a written response (a
“Response Notice”) in which the Indemnifying Party shall with respect to a Non-Third Party Claim
(i) agree that all of the Non-Third Party Claim is owed to the Indemnified Party (the “Agreed
Amount Notice”), (ii) agree that part, but not all, of the Non-Third Party Claim is owed to the
Indemnified Party (the “Partial Agreed Amount Notice”), or (iii) contest that any of the Non-
Third Party Claim is owed to the Indemnified Party (the “Contest Notice”). If no Response Notice
is delivered by the Indemnifying Party by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the last day of such thirty
(30) day period (such 30-day period commencing upon receipt by the Indemnifying Party of an
Indemnity Claim Notice), Indemnifying Party shall be deemed to have agreed that all of the amount
of the Non-Third Party Claim must be paid to the Indemnified Party and in such case, the Claim
shall be treated as if an Agreed Amount Notice was furnished.

       19.6    Third Party Claims.

Within thirty (30) days after receipt of an Indemnity Claim Notice, the Indemnifying Party shall
furnish to the Indemnified Party a Response Notice in which the Indemnifying Party shall with
respect to a Third Party Claim (i) agree that it is responsible to defend and indemnify any liability
arising under such Third Party Claim (a “Defense Notice”), or (ii) disagree that it is responsible to
defend and indemnify any liability arising under such Third Party Claim. If the Indemnifying
Party gives a Defense Notice, it will undertake the defense of the Claim by representatives of its
own choosing reasonably satisfactory to the Indemnified Party. Indemnified Party shall have the
right at its own expense to participate in any such defense with representatives of its own choosing.

                (a)     Notwithstanding anything contained herein to the contrary, the Indemnified
Party shall be entitled to participate, with counsel of its choosing and its own expense, in the
defense, settlement, adjustment or compromise of (but the Indemnifying Party shall nevertheless
be required to pay all Damages incurred by the Indemnified Party in connection with such defense,
settlement or compromise, as required by this Article) any Third Party Claim (i) that seeks an
order, injunction or other equitable relief against the Indemnified Party or any of its Affiliates; (ii)
for which the Indemnified Party would otherwise be entitled to indemnification under this Article,
and (iii) in which both the Indemnifying Party and the Indemnified Party are named as parties and
either the Indemnifying Party or the Indemnified Party determines with advice of counsel that there
may be one or more legal defenses available to it that are different from or additional to those
available to the other party or that a conflict of interest between such parties may exist in respect
thereto, in which event Indemnifying Party and Indemnified Party shall reasonably cooperate in
such defense, but the Indemnified Party shall have final control over any injunctive relief brought
against it, and any different or additional legal defense specifically available only to it, and
Indemnifying Party shall have final control over all other aspects of the Third Party Claim.

               (b)     Each party shall make available to the other party and its attorneys and
accountants, at all reasonable times during normal business hours, all books, records, and other


                                                  40

===== PAGE 83 =====
documents in its possession relating to such Third Party Claim. The party contesting any such
Third Party Claim shall be furnished all reasonable assistance in connection therewith by the other
party.

               (c)     Subject to Section 19.6(a) hereto, the Indemnifying Party shall not, without
the Indemnified Party’s written consent, settle or compromise any Third Party Claim or consent to
entry of any judgment which does not include as an unconditional term thereof the giving by the
claimant or the plaintiff to Indemnified Party an unconditional release from all liability in respect
of such Third Party Claim.

                (d)    If the Indemnifying Party fails to timely give a Defense Notice or thereafter
fails to timely undertake the defense of, or settle or pay, any such Third-Party Claim, then the
Indemnified Party may take any and all necessary action to dispose of such Third-Party Claim,
including, without limitation, the settlement or full payment thereof upon such terms as it shall
deem appropriate, in its sole discretion.

       19.7 Reimbursement. Subject to the provisions of this Article XIX, the Indemnified
Party shall be reimbursed by the Indemnifying Party on demand, for any Damages or any Claim
to which this Article XIX relates.

        19.8 Limitation on Indemnification. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 19.1,
the Selling Parties shall not be required to indemnify Purchaser Parties or any of its directors,
officers, members, partners, shareholders or employees unless the aggregate of all amounts for
which any indemnity would otherwise be payable by the Selling Parties under Section 19.1 above
exceeds $10,000 (the “Minimum Claim Amount”) (b) in no event shall the liability of Selling
Parties with respect to the indemnification provided for in Section 19.1 above exceed in the
aggregate $1,500,000.00 (the “Maximum Liability Amount”), except for any claims arising out of
the fraud of intentional misconduct of Current Operator or Seller, or claims related to Recapture,
CARES Act Payments, or Medicaid Advance Payments, which shall not be subject to the
Maximum Liability Amount, and (c) if prior to the Closing, Purchaser or New Operator obtains
knowledge of any inaccuracy or breach of any representation, warranty or covenant of Current
Operator contained in this Agreement (a “Purchaser Waived Breach”) and nonetheless proceeds
with and consummates the Closing, then Purchaser Parties shall be deemed to have waived and
forever renounced any right to assert a claim for indemnification for that specific inaccuracy or
breach on account of any such Purchaser Waived Breach under this Section 19, or for any other
claim or cause of action under this Agreement for that specific inaccuracy or breach, at law or in
equity.

       19.9 Exclusive Remedy. Notwithstanding anything contained in this Agreement to the
contrary, Purchaser and the Selling Parties acknowledge and agree that the indemnification
provisions set forth in this Article XIX and Section 6.5 shall be the sole and exclusive remedy of
Purchaser Parties and the Selling Parties with respect to (i) any claim for breach of any
representations, warranties, covenants, agreements or other obligations or provisions of this
Agreement and any indemnities provided for herein, and (ii) the Assets and the transactions
contemplated by this Agreement.

consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, neither Purchaser Parties nor
Selling Parties (or any of their respective Affiliates) shall, and each shall direct their agents and
representatives not to, directly or indirectly, make any public comment, statement or

information of the other party, except that such comments, statements, communications and
disclosures may be made by each of the Purchaser Parties and Selling Parties (a) to such of their
agents and representatives as need to know such information for the purpose of evaluating or
otherwise effecting the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (b) if it is required to do so
by applicable Laws, provided that one party shall notify the other parties in advance in writing of
any such disclosure, (c) to Governmental Authorities and their agents as appropriate, and (d) for
the purposes of obtaining Consents. Except with respect to subparagraph (c) above, if a party is
required by Law to make any such disclosure, it shall provide the other party the contents of the

any such disclosure prior to making such disclosure.

        20.21 Confidentiality. Except as otherwise required by court order, each party hereto
and its agents, representatives and employees shall protect and maintain the confidentiality of all
matters related to and contemplated by this Agreement and the agreements executed and delivered
in connection herewith (“Confidential Matters”). Furthermore, each party shall use its
commercially reasonable efforts to cause its representatives and agents to protect and maintain the
confidentiality of all Confidential Matters. Each party agrees to reveal any Confidential Matters
only to its representatives, agents and employees who need to know such Confidential Matters for

confidential nature of such Confidential Matters, and who agree to act in accordance with the terms
of this Section 20.21. Nothing in this Section 20.21 shall prevent a party from disclosing or
permitting the disclosure of Confidential Matters if compelled to do so by court order or other
requirement of Law or in accordance with this Agreement. If a party receives a court order
compelling disclosure of Confidential Matters, it shall promptly notify the other parties so that
such parties may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy. The confidentiality
obligations set forth in this Section shall survive any termination of this Agreement for a period of
twelve (12) months from the later of: (a) twelve (12) months following the Closing Date or (b)
termination of this Agreement pursuant to Article XVII above.

                                           PROMISSORY NOTE

$500,000.00                                                                                          [●], 2026

         THIS PROMISSORY NOTE (this “Note”) by 55 SCALLOP SHELL, LLC, a Rhode Island
limited liability company (“Purchaser”) and ADVINIACARE SCALLOP SHELL, LLC, a Rhode Island
limited liability company, (“New Operator” and together with Purchaser, “Borrower”) is made payable to,
or to the order of, 981 KINGS TOWN ROAD, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, (the “Seller”)
and 981 KINGS TOWN ROAD OPERATING COMPANY, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company,
(“Current Operator” and together with the Seller, “Lender”).

1. PROMISE TO PAY. For value received, Borrower hereby promises to pay to the order of Lender at
its address set forth above or at such other place as may be designated, from time to time, in writing by
Lender, in lawful money of the United States of America, the principal sum of Five Hundred Thousand and
00/100 Dollars ($500,000.00), together with interest on the unpaid principal balance thereof computed from
the date hereof at the rate of six percent (6%) per annum, pursuant to the terms of this Note. Upon an Event
of Default, the interest rate shall increase by five percent (5%), until Borrower’s cure of the Event of Default
to the sole satisfaction of Lender.

2. PAYMENT. Borrower shall repay principal and interest in thirty-six (36) monthly installments as
follows: (a) thirty-five (35) monthly installment payments of interest only on the unpaid principal balance
of this Note, with the first of such installments to become due on [●], 2026, and, (b) the final 36th monthly
installment in an amount equal to the total amount of the unpaid principal balance of this Note and all
interest and all other accrued charges and other amounts owed pursuant to this Note that remain unpaid. If
Borrower fails to pay, within five (5) days of its due date, any amount due and owing pursuant to this Note,
Borrower shall immediately pay to Lender a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the delinquent amount.
If, from any circumstance whatsoever, fulfillment of any provision of this Note at the time performance of
such provision shall be due, shall involve exceeding any usury limit prescribed by law which a court of
competent jurisdiction may deem applicable hereto, then, ipso facto, the obligations to be fulfilled shall be
reduced to allow compliance with such limit, and if, from any circumstance whatsoever, Lender shall ever
receive as interest an amount which would exceed the highest lawful rate, the receipt of such excess shall
be deemed a mistake and shall be canceled automatically or, if theretofore paid, such excess shall be
credited against the principal amount of the indebtedness evidenced hereby to which the same may be
lawfully credited, and any portion of such excess not capable of being so credited shall be immediately
refunded to Borrower without interest.

3. PREPAYMENT. Borrower shall have the option of prepaying all or any portion of the outstanding
principal amount at any time and from time to time without premium or penalty resulting from such
prepayment; provided, Borrower provides Lender with not less than ten (10) days prior written notice of
such prepayment and, that upon a prepayment in full Borrower shall pay all interest and other amounts then
owing and payable under to this Note and remaining unpaid.

4. EVENT OF DEFAULT. An “Event of Default” occurs or exists if: (i) Borrower defaults in the payment
when due of any principal or any interest or other amount payable pursuant to this Note and such default
continues unremedied for five (5) calendar days, (ii) Borrower has any receiver, trustee, custodian or similar
person for it or any of its assets appointed (whether with or without its consent), makes any assignment for
the benefit of creditors or commences or has commenced against it any bankruptcy or insolvency
proceeding or any formal or informal proceeding for the dissolution, liquidation or winding up of the affairs
of or the settlement of claims against it, and, in the event of any such proceeding commenced against it,
such proceeding is not stayed or dismissed within sixty (60) days after the commencement thereof or any
such stay is lifted; (iii) any event of default shall have occurred under the Guaranty by and among Lender,

                                                           GUARANTY

In consideration of 981 KINGS TOWN ROAD, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the “Seller”) and 981 KINGS
TOWN ROAD OPERATING COMPANY, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Current Operator” and together
with the Seller, “Lender”) extending or agreeing to extend any credit or other financial accommodation to 55 SCALLOP
SHELL, LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability (“Purchaser”) and ADVINIACARE SCALLOP SHELL, LLC, a Rhode
Island limited liability company (“New Operator” and together with Purchaser, “Borrower”) or (b) agreeing to any direct or
indirect extension, renewal, refinancing or other modification or replacement of or waiving or forbearing from exercising any
right or remedy relating to any obligation heretofore or hereafter arising or accruing as a result of any such credit or other
financial accommodation, and for other valuable consideration, the receipt of which is acknowledged, Yosef Meystel, an
individual (“YM”), David Berkowitz, an individual (“DB”) and Benjamin Berkowitz, an individual (“BB” and together with
YM and DB collectively, jointly and severally the “Guarantors”, and each individually, a “Guarantor”) agrees with Lender
as follows:

1.       CAPITALIZED TERMS. Capitalized terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning ascribed to them
in the Purchase Agreement.

2.       GUARANTY.

         (a)       Each Guarantor unconditionally guarantees, without any setoff or other deduction, the payment when due,
whether by acceleration or lapse of time or otherwise, of the Obligations, as defined below. This Guaranty (as amended,
supplemented or otherwise modified, the “Guaranty”) is a continuing, absolute, irrevocable and unconditional guaranty of
payment and not collection. “Obligations” means, collectively, all obligations of Borrower to Lender pursuant to that (i) certain
Note from Borrower to Lender dated on or about the date hereof in the original principal amount of $500,000.00 (as the same
may be amended, restated, increased, replaced, extended or otherwise modified, the “Note”), and (ii) any other document or
instrument delivered in connection therewith, in any capacity for the payment of any money, regardless of kind, class or form,
whether for the payment of any principal, interest, fee, charge, cost or expense or otherwise (including, without limitation, to
the extent permitted by Law, reasonable attorneys’ fees and legal expenses), now existing or hereafter arising or accruing,
created directly or by any assignment or other transfer, direct or indirect, absolute or contingent (whether pursuant to any
guaranty, endorsement or other assurance of payment or otherwise), whether similar or dissimilar or related or unrelated and
whether or not arising or accrued subsequent to any commencement of or made, proved, voted or allowed as a claim in any
case or other proceeding pursuant to any bankruptcy, insolvency or similar statute, that have been heretofore or are hereafter
incurred by, in any capacity and whether alone or otherwise, Borrower or, if Borrower is not an individual, any direct or indirect
successor of Borrower or any direct or indirect transferee of all or substantially all of the assets of Borrower together with all
amendments, extensions, renewals or increases thereof.

          (b)       Each portion of the Obligations now or hereafter (i) paid or satisfied or (ii) received, applied or retained by
Lender and later recovered from Lender as a result of any claim (including, without limitation, any claim involving any
allegation that any money constituted trust funds or that the receipt, application or retention of any payments or the grant,
creation or perfection of any security interest or lien on any collateral constituted a preference or a fraudulent conveyance or
transfer), shall be reinstated as part of the Obligations for purposes of this Guaranty as of the date it originally arose or accrued.

3.        INDEMNIFICATION. Each Guarantor shall indemnify, defend and hold Lender and their respective directors,
officers, members, partners, shareholders, agents and employees harmless at all times from and after the date hereof on demand,
without any limitation as to amount, against each liability, cost and expense (including, but not limited to, if Lender retains
counsel for advice, litigation or any other purpose related to this Guaranty, reasonable attorneys’ fees and disbursements)
heretofore or hereafter imposed on, incurred by or asserted against Lender as a result of any actions, suits, proceedings, claims,
demands, assessments, judgment, or litigation arising out of this Guaranty.

4.       EXPENSES. Guarantors shall pay to Lender on demand each cost and expense (including, but not limited to, if
Lender retains counsel for advice, litigation or any other purpose, reasonable attorneys’ fees and disbursements) hereafter
incurred by Lender in endeavoring to enforce any obligation of Guarantors pursuant to this Guaranty or preserve or exercise
any right or remedy of Lender pursuant to this Guaranty.

5.       FURNISHING OF INFORMATION. Promptly upon the request of Lender, Guarantors shall furnish to Lender all
information requested by Lender and relating to Guarantors or the business, operations, assets, affairs or condition of each
respective Guarantor.

6.        POSTPONEMENT OF SUBROGATION. Until (a) the final and indefeasible payment in full of (i) the Obligations,
and (ii) each liability, cost and expense that Guarantors are obligated to pay pursuant to this Guaranty and (b) the expiration or
other termination of each commitment and other agreement of Lender to extend any credit or other financial accommodation
to Borrower, no Guarantor shall assert any claim against Borrower or any other Guarantor or commence or prosecute any action
or other legal proceeding relating to or otherwise enforce any right of subrogation, indemnification, reimbursement or
contribution, or any similar right, against Borrower or any other Guarantor in connection with this Guaranty or any of the
Obligations or any collateral therefore.

7.      TERMINATION. This Guaranty shall remain in full force and effect until the Obligations and any liability, cost and
expense that Guarantors are obligated to pay pursuant to this Guaranty have been indefeasibly paid in full.

notice, and agrees that this Guaranty shall not be modified or terminated as to each Guarantor by, or no right or remedy shall
be waived by, whether now in existence or hereafter occurring, (A) any direct or indirect extension, renewal, refinancing or
other modification or replacement of, or any assignment or other transfer, compromise, cancellation, discharge, invalidity,

corporation, partnership, limited liability company, governmental body or other entity who or that is now or hereafter liable,

interest in or other lien on any collateral for the Obligations, (E) any exercise or waiver of, failure or delaying to exercise,

                    RECORDS TRANSFER AND ACCESS AGREEMENT

         This Records Transfer and Access Agreement (the “Agreement”), dated as of [●], 2026, is
made by and between 981 Kings Town Road Operating Company, LLC, a Delaware limited
liability company (“Transferor”) and Adviniacare Scallop Shell, LLC, a Rhode Island limited
liability company (“Transferee”). Transferor and Transferee may hereinafter collectively be referred
to as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party”.

       WHEREAS, Transferor is the lessee and licensed operator of a certain 80 bed skilled
nursing facility commonly known as “Elderwood of Scallop Shell at Wakefield,” located at 55
Scallop Shell Way, Wakefield, Rhode Island (the “Facility”); and

       WHEREAS, the Parties hereto have executed a Purchase and Sale Agreement dated as of
December 23, 2025 (the “Purchase Agreement”) whereby the Selling Parties have agreed,
subject to the terms and conditions contained therein, to sell the Assets of the Facility and Real
Property to the Purchaser Parties; and

        WHEREAS, the Purchase Agreement provides for the transfer of all files, charts, and other
Resident information (i) in Transferor’s possession or control relating to all Residents occupying
or using the Facility on the Closing Date, or (ii) who previously occupied or used the Facility prior
to the Closing Date and who are not Residents of the Facility on the Closing Date; and

       WHEREAS, the Parties desire to arrange for an orderly process for the transfer of custody of
Transferor’s Records to Transferee to provide continuity of care for the Residents at the Facility and
provide for Transferor’s continued access to the Records for legal and business purposes.

        NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth
in this Agreement, as well as other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of
which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

1.     Capitalized Terms. Capitalized terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning
ascribed to them in the Purchase Agreement.

2.     Transfer and Custody of Records.

                A. Upon the consummation of the transactions contemplated in the Purchase
Agreement (the “Effective Date”), Transferor will transfer physical possession of all files, charts,
and other Resident information in Transferor’s possession or control relating to (i) all Residents
occupying or using the Facility on the Closing Date, and (ii) all Residents who previously occupied
or used the Facility prior to the Closing Date and who are not Residents of the Facility on the
Closing Date (the “Records”). Transferor will not be required to maintain copies of the Records
transferred to Transferee under this Agreement.

               B. Transferee agrees to accept, maintain and preserve custody of the Records at its
sole cost and expense, and assume all of the custodial responsibilities with respect to the Records



                                                  1

===== PAGE 140 =====
for a minimum of six (6) years from the Closing Date or other minimum period as prescribed by
Law. Transferee may elect to retain any Record for a longer period, at its discretion.

                C. Transferee agrees to maintain the Records in accordance with all applicable state
and federal laws, rules and regulations governing confidentiality and security of patient medical
records, including but not limited to the requirements of the Standards for Privacy of Individually
Identifiable Health Information published by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
at 45 C.F.R. part 160 and part 164, subpart E, under the Health Insurance Portability and
Accountability Act of 1996 (42 U.S.C. 1320d-1329d-8), as amended from time to time, including
by the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act (42 U.S.C. 3000 et
seq.) (collectively, the “HIPAA”). Transferee is hereby deemed to be a “business associate” of
Transferor as that term is defined in HIPAA. As such, as of the Effective Date, the parties have
entered into a Business Associate Agreement, attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated by
reference herein.

                D. Transferee and its staff will not access any Record, or permit access by any other
individual or entity, unless such access is permitted by Law. Transferee will not alter, or permit
alteration of, any entry or documentation in the Records relating to treatment or services provided
on or before the Effective Date.

              E. If any patient requests an amendment to their Record for services provided prior
to the Effective Date, Transferee will comply with such request in accordance with the
requirements of all relevant Laws.

                F. Transferee will provide reasonable access, upon reasonable notice and during
normal business hours, to make copies of the Records, to, and copies of, any Record to the patient
who is the subject of the Record or their authorized representative to the extent required by Law
or regulation, and to all other individuals, entities, and governmental agencies that have the right
to access or receive copies of the Records under the applicable Laws and regulations.

                G. The Parties understand and agree that Transferor is and will remain legally
responsible for all entries and documents placed in the Records for care and treatment provided
prior to the Effective Date.

               H. If a Resident requests that Transferee transfer their Record to a physician or an
entity who is not an employee of or affiliated with Transferee, Transferee will retain the original
Record and provide the Resident or Resident’s designee with a copy of the Record.

               I. Transferee may, at its discretion, transfer the Records to microfilm or similar
medium, or to an electronic medical record system or other electronic format, and destroy the
original paper Records, so long as the integrity of the contents of the Records is maintained.


3.     Access to Records.




                                                 2

===== PAGE 141 =====
                A. For Transferor’s legal or business purposes, Transferor shall be entitled to
inspect, at Transferee’s premises or another mutually agreed location and during normal business
hours, and to make copies of the Records while they are in the possession of Transferee.

                 B. The Parties acknowledge and agree that such purposes may include, but shall
not be limited to, Transferor’s pursuit of reimbursement for services it rendered to patients and to
the extent reasonably necessary to enable Transferor to among other things investigate and defend
malpractice, employee or other claims, to support medical review requests from Medicare or
Medicaid, to support Medicare and Medicaid claims appeals, to file or defend cost reports and Tax
returns, to complete/revise, as needed, any patient assessments which may be required for
Transferor to seek reimbursement for services rendered prior to the Closing Date, to verify
accounts receivable collections due Transferor, to file exceptions to the Medicare or Medicaid
routine cost limits for the cost reporting periods prior to the Closing Date and to enable Transferor
to complete, in accordance with Transferor’s policies and procedures, any and all post-Closing
Date accounting, reconciliation and closing procedures, including, but not limited to, a month end
close out of all accounts, including but not limited to accounts payable and Medicare and Medicaid
billing; provided, however, that Transferor shall maintain the confidentiality of the information in
such Records in the same manner as it did prior to the transfer effected hereunder. Transferee shall
respond promptly and cooperate actively with Transferor’s requests for inspection or copies.

4.      Term and Termination.

              A. This Agreement will take effect on the Effective Date and will remain in effect
through the date when all of the Records have been destroyed, unless terminated earlier as
described below.

                  B. This Agreement may be terminated at any time by the mutual written consent
of the Parties.

               C. In the event the Parties agree to terminate this Agreement prior to the destruction
of all Records, the Parties will fully cooperate with each other to ensure the prompt return of the
Records to the proper Party.

                 B. Neither Party will be authorized to act as agent for the other Party or to incur
